Gardens of the Test Server

The garden behind the test server has grown for many seasons. Every spring the gardener plants rows of beans, peas and tall sunflowers, and every autumn she writes down what grew well and what the slugs ate before anyone could pick it.

This year the beds were laid out in a new pattern, drawn in the diagram above. The paths run north to south so the morning light reaches every row, and the compost sits in the corner nearest the kitchen door.

Lazy pictures

Some pictures on this page load only when a reader scrolls to them, and the clipper has to find their real address in an attribute the browser would have read.

Code in the shed

The watering timer in the shed runs a short program every morning at six.

# water the beans first
for bed in beds:
    water(bed, minutes=4)

When it rains, the timer skips the run and logs the skip in a notebook that nobody reads.
